idiom_name: boundary module with explicit toLegacy / fromLegacy mappers
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the shape is just data, so a window is a small module exporting two pure functions - fromLegacy() to the canonical model and toLegacy() back - rather than a class hierarchy; JSON.parse/JSON.stringify do the encoding, with a replacer or toJSON() only where the old payload trims or renames fields. A Proxy wrapper is worth it only when the legacy surface is a wide object whose members must keep their old names, since the trap handlers let forwarding be centralised the way the Proxy documentation describes. The classic hand-written mapper remains the honest choice when the legacy format is not JSON at all (fixed width, EBCDIC, COBOL copybooks), where Buffer parsing replaces serialization entirely.
pitfalls: Number handling is where old shapes break: JavaScript floats versus legacy fixed-point fields, and JSON.stringify turning NaN or Infinity into null without complaint.
Mappers that hand back the same nested objects the core holds let legacy callers mutate canonical state through the old API; copy at the boundary.
Old clients often parse error strings and status codes, so throwing a new-style Error changes the contract as much as renaming a field does.
